topic: POV finder pain quote: 'the factory says it's certified' but the PDF is a GCC with in-house testing; children's products need third-party testing (1107.20(a)) and a CPC (1110.3)
hook_formula: pain quote (playbook: 'The factory says it's certified. The PDF doesn't say what they think it says.')
vo: Say the factory says it's certified. The PDF doesn't say what you think.
Then I open the PDF. General certificate. In-house test.
Kids' products usually need third-party lab testing and a children's product certificate.
So I check which rules apply first.
Not sure which rules apply? Free C P S C finder. See which rules apply. No account needed.
caption:
"It's certified," says the factory. Then the PDF turns out to be a general certificate backed by an in-house test.
For a children's product, 16 CFR 1107.20(a) has manufacturers send samples to a third party conformity assessment body for testing to support certification.
And the certificate for a children's product is a Children's Product Certificate (CPC), not a General Certificate of Conformity (16 CFR 1110.3).
Say a seller only has the factory's GCC for kids' backpacks. Checking which rules apply is the first step.

sources.claim: Children's products: samples to a third party conformity assessment body for testing to support certification
sources.quote: (a) Manufacturers must submit a sufficient number of samples of a children's product, or samples that are identical in all material respects to the children's product, to a third party conformity assessment body for testing to support certification.

sources.claim: CPC is the certificate for children's products; GCC for general-use (section 14(a)(1))
sources.quote: Children's Product Certificate (CPC) means a certificate of compliance for a finished product issued pursuant to section 14(a)(2) of the CPSA, 15 U.S.C. 2063, and part 1107 of this chapter. ... General Certificate of Conformity (GCC) means a certificate of compliance for a finished product issued pursuant to section 14(a)(1) of the CPSA, 15 U.S.C. 2063(a)(1).
